title: Consolidate mid-cycle credit attribution and export sanity checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem summary: Several customers reported invoice mismatches after mid-cycle plan changes and late-arriving rate-limit credit adjustments. Root cause analysis shows two interacting issues: (1) asynchronous credit events (rate-limit refunds and promo adjustments) are bucketed by event_timestamp rather than the customer's billing interval window used for invoice line allocation, causing credits to attach to the wrong invoice cycle when they cross UTC boundaries; (2) our Stripe->NetSuite export job merges line items using a timestamp-based dedupe that doesn't consider proration anchors (plan_change_at) resulting in merged lines that under- or over-credit customers when a plan change occurs mid-cycle.

Scope and goals: 1) Ensure credits/refunds are attributed to the correct invoice/billing period in the NetSuite export. 2) Avoid double-counting or losing proration adjustments when usage corrections arrive after plan change. 3) Add export-level sanity checks and alerting to detect divergent invoice totals (>0.5% drift) compared to Stripe net amounts. 4) Provide a backfill path to correct affected historical exports and generate NetSuite adjustment entries where needed.

Technical approach: - Export job change: switch from event_timestamp bucketing to using the customer's billing_period_anchor (billing_period_start, billing_period_end) that is derived from subscription.start_date and proration anchors. When an adjustment references a subscription_id, map the adjustment to the billing interval it should apply to using the subscription timeline rather than the raw event time. - Merge logic: introduce a deterministic key for invoice-line merges that includes (customer_id, billing_period_start, adjustment_reason_code, plan_change_anchor). This prevents mixing pre- and post-plan-change adjustments. - Timezone edgecases: normalize all interval math to UTC but compute anchors using subscription metadata to handle customer-specific billing anchor offsets. - Sanity checks: compute reconciled_amount = stripe_net_amount - exported_netsuite_amount; publish a reconciliation metric per-customer and per-export-run; fire pager alert if abs(reconciled_amount) / stripe_net_amount > 0.005 for customers with monthly revenue > $1k. - Backfill: a 2-step backfill job (dry-run then write) that recomputes invoice line allocations for affected invoice ranges and emits NetSuite credit/debit memo drafts. Backfill will be gated by a manual approval workflow in the Console (billing ops) and include an idempotent signature so repeated runs do not duplicate memos.

Implementation tasks: - SQL: add function map_adjustment_to_billing_anchor(subscription_id, adjustment_time) and rewrite hourly_aggregator to join on billing_anchor instead of event_bucket. - Exporter: update stripe_exporter.go to compute merge_key and attach anchor metadata in export payload. - Reconciler: new reconciliation microservice (billing-reconciler) that compares Stripe net to NetSuite export, records diffs, and exposes dashboard metrics. - Tests: unit tests for mapping logic, integration tests with replayed Stripe webhook fixtures (promo, rate-limit-credit, invoice.updated), e2e test that runs full export + netsuite-stub. - Observability: Grafana dashboard with per-run histograms, and alerting rules in PagerDuty.

Acceptance criteria: - New exporter produces same number of non-merged invoice lines for historical non-edge cases (to ensure no regressions), and correctly re-assigns at least 95% of previously-misaligned credits in a staging backfill. - Reconciliation metric exists and alerts trigger in staging for intentionally injected mismatch. - Backfill produces memo drafts and a safety report for ops. - No customer-facing invoices are modified automatically without an ops-approved backfill run.

Migration plan and rollout: 1) Deploy exporter changes behind feature flag; enable reconciler in read-only mode for 1 week to gather coverage. 2) Run targeted dry-run backfills for top 10 impacted customers identified in signal to validate. 3) After ops sign-off, run write-mode backfill for remaining affected invoices in batches, monitor reconciler metrics and customer complaints. 4) Flip feature flag for live exports and monitor for 48 hours with elevated alerting.

Longer-term notes: Consider moving to a single canonical billing window service that other components can query so mapping logic is not duplicated across exporters and the invoicing pipeline. Also evaluate whether using invoice-level canonical IDs from Stripe (invoice.id) rather than subscription-based anchors would simplify mapping for certain promo cases.
